title: The Alaska Highway breaks through
photoNote: Corporal Refines Sims Jr. (97th Engineers, left) and Private Alfred Jalufka (18th Engineers) shake hands at the meeting of the bulldozers near Beaver Creek, Yukon, 25 October 1942. Taken by Harold W. Richardson of Engineering News-Record; public domain on Wikimedia Commons. Three days before the card's date.
body:
Two bulldozer drivers, one Black and one white, crashed through the Yukon woods toward each other. The photo of their handshake was printed across the country.

28 October 1942. The Army declared the pioneer road of the Alaska Highway finished: more than 1,500 miles from Dawson Creek, British Columbia, to Delta Junction, Alaska, cut through wilderness in about eight months.

Three days earlier, near Beaver Creek, Corporal Refines Sims Jr. of the 97th Engineers met Private Alfred Jalufka of the 18th Engineers, their two crews finally joined. The 97th was one of three African American regiments on the project.

The road built to supply Alaska in wartime is still driven today.

#OnThisDay #WW2
